messages.content:
New machine. Its objects are: zekuror, nonogok, mikazak, lonigos, sirimi, firomu.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half the objects. This splits the 30 possibilities (15 pairs × 2 rules) evenly into 15 that would light up and 15 that would not.

TEST: zekuror, nonogok, mikazak
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

Remaining possibilities: if one nexiom is enough, both must be among lonigos, sirimi and firomu, which gives 3 pairs. If both are needed, any pair except the ones lying entirely within the first group is possible, which gives 12 pairs. That makes 15 possibilities in total.

Testing zekuror, nonogok, lonigos and sirimi lights up in 8 of them and stays dark in 7. That is close to an even split.

TEST: zekuror, nonogok, lonigos, sirimi
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The first two dark results rule out the one-nexiom rule. If one nexiom were enough, both nexioms would have to avoid both tested groups, and only firomu is outside both, so two nexioms can't fit. The machine therefore needs **two**.

With the two-nexiom rule, a test stays dark unless it contains both nexioms. That eliminates every pair lying entirely inside either tested group. Seven pairs remain:
- zekuror + firomu
- nonogok + firomu
- mikazak + firomu
- lonigos + firomu
- sirimi + firomu
- mikazak + lonigos
- mikazak + sirimi

Testing mikazak, lonigos and firomu lights up for 3 of these (mikazak + firomu, lonigos + firomu, mikazak + lonigos). It stays dark for the other 4.

TEST: mikazak, lonigos, firomu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The third dark result rules out mikazak + firomu, lonigos + firomu and mikazak + lonigos. The machine needs two nexioms, so four pairs remain:
- zekuror + firomu
- nonogok + firomu
- sirimi + firomu
- mikazak + sirimi

Testing zekuror, sirimi and firomu splits these evenly. It lights up for zekuror + firomu and sirimi + firomu, and stays dark for nonogok + firomu and mikazak + sirimi. One more test after this will settle which pair it is.

TEST: zekuror, sirimi, firomu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

The fourth dark result rules out zekuror + firomu and sirimi + firomu. Two pairs remain:
- nonogok + firomu
- mikazak + sirimi

The rule is still certainly "needs two". Together the four dark tests covered all six objects, so under a one-nexiom rule something would have lit.

Testing nonogok and firomu settles it. If it lights, those are the nexioms; if it stays dark, the pair is mikazak + sirimi.

TEST: nonogok, firomu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The fifth dark result rules out nonogok + firomu, so the only possibility left is **mikazak + sirimi**. This fits every test: none of the five tests had mikazak and sirimi on the machine together, so all stayed dark.

The rule must be "needs two". The dark tests together covered all six objects, so under a one-nexiom rule at least one test would have lit up.

ANSWER: nexioms = mikazak, sirimi; needs = two

messages.content:
New machine. Its objects are: bavonak, sugudik, zabale, dadivel, futivun, rutazi.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to split the possibilities.

TEST: bavonak, sugudik, zabale
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

The first test ruled out a lot. If the machine needs one nexiom, both nexioms must be among dadivel, futivun and rutazi. If it needs two, any pair is still possible except a pair inside bavonak, sugudik and zabale. That leaves 15 possibilities. Testing dadivel, futivun and rutazi splits them about 6 to 9, which is the most even split I can get from one test.

TEST: dadivel, futivun, rutazi
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The second test lit up, so in either mode both nexioms must be among dadivel, futivun and rutazi. That leaves six possibilities: the pair is dadivel+futivun, dadivel+rutazi or futivun+rutazi, and the machine needs either one or two. Testing dadivel alone splits these: it lights up only if the machine needs one nexiom and dadivel is one of them.

TEST: dadivel
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Dadivel alone did not light up, so four possibilities remain:
1. Futivun and rutazi are the nexioms, and the machine needs one.
2. Dadivel and futivun are the nexioms, and the machine needs two.
3. Dadivel and rutazi are the nexioms, and the machine needs two.
4. Futivun and rutazi are the nexioms, and the machine needs two.

Testing dadivel and futivun together lights up only in cases 1 and 2, so it splits the four evenly. One more test can then separate whichever two are left.

TEST: dadivel, futivun
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Dadivel and futivun together did not light up, so cases 1 and 2 are out. The machine needs two nexioms, and rutazi is one of them. The other is either dadivel or futivun. Testing dadivel and rutazi together will settle it: it lights up only if they are the pair.

TEST: dadivel, rutazi
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Dadivel and rutazi together did not light up, so only one possibility is left. Futivun and rutazi are the nexioms, and the machine needs both of them together. This fits every result: the only test that lit up was the one with both futivun and rutazi on it. Every other test had at most one of them.

ANSWER: nexioms = futivun, rutazi; needs = two

messages.content:
New machine. Its objects are: mukabo, dezisu, lefuvan, ketises, fedagil, febanan.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half the objects. This splits the 30 possible cases (15 pairs × 2 rules) evenly.

TEST: mukabo, dezisu, lefuvan
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

Since that test stayed dark, two cases remain. Under the "needs one" rule, mukabo, dezisu and lefuvan are all non-nexioms, so the pair is inside {ketises, fedagil, febanan}, which gives 3 options. Under the "needs two" rule, the pair is anything except a pair taken entirely from the first three objects, which gives 12 options. That makes 15 possibilities in total.

Testing mukabo, dezisu, ketises and fedagil splits these 15 roughly in half:
- **Lights up (8 cases):** all 3 "needs one" pairs, plus 5 "needs two" pairs (mukabo–ketises, mukabo–fedagil, dezisu–ketises, dezisu–fedagil, ketises–fedagil).
- **Stays dark (7 cases):** the remaining "needs two" pairs.

TEST: mukabo, dezisu, ketises, fedagil
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The "needs one" rule is now ruled out. If only one nexiom were needed, the first test would make mukabo, dezisu and lefuvan non-nexioms. The second test would also rule out ketises and fedagil. That leaves only febanan, but there must be two nexioms. So this machine **needs two**.

Under "needs two", the pair cannot lie entirely within either earlier test set. That leaves 7 possible pairs:
- febanan paired with mukabo, dezisu, lefuvan, ketises or fedagil (5 pairs)
- lefuvan–ketises or lefuvan–fedagil (2 pairs)

Testing febanan, mukabo, dezisu and lefuvan splits these as evenly as possible:
- **Lights up (3 pairs):** mukabo–febanan, dezisu–febanan, lefuvan–febanan
- **Stays dark (4 pairs):** ketises–febanan, fedagil–febanan, lefuvan–ketises, lefuvan–fedagil

TEST: febanan, mukabo, dezisu, lefuvan
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine lit up, so under the "needs two" rule both nexioms were among febanan, mukabo, dezisu and lefuvan. Of the 7 pairs still possible, that leaves 3:
- mukabo–febanan
- dezisu–febanan
- lefuvan–febanan

Febanan must be one of the nexioms, so I'll test febanan with mukabo:
- **Lights up:** the pair is mukabo–febanan.
- **Stays dark:** the pair is dezisu–febanan or lefuvan–febanan, and one more test will settle it.

TEST: febanan, mukabo
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Febanan with mukabo stayed dark, so mukabo is not the second nexiom. That leaves two possible pairs:
- dezisu–febanan
- lefuvan–febanan

Testing febanan with dezisu settles it:
- **Lights up:** the pair is dezisu–febanan.
- **Stays dark:** the pair is lefuvan–febanan.

TEST: febanan, dezisu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Febanan with dezisu stayed dark, so dezisu is not the second nexiom. The only remaining pair is lefuvan–febanan, which fits every result:
- **Test 1** (mukabo, dezisu, lefuvan): only lefuvan was present, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 2** (mukabo, dezisu, ketises, fedagil): neither nexiom was present, so it stayed dark.
- **Test 3** (febanan, mukabo, dezisu, lefuvan): both nexioms were present, so it lit up.
- **Tests 4 and 5:** only febanan was present, so both stayed dark.

Test 2 also showed that the machine needs both nexioms. No further test is needed.

ANSWER: nexioms = lefuvan, febanan; needs = two

messages.content:
New machine. Its objects are: fusinun, napofe, zuzalan, pukenon, somonil, mesuvir.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half the objects, since that splits the 30 possible answers (15 pairs × 2 rules) evenly whichever way it comes out.

TEST: fusinun, napofe, zuzalan
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

The first test ruled out a lot. If one nexiom is enough, both nexioms must be among pukenon, somonil and mesuvir (3 possibilities). If both are needed, any pair except one entirely within fusinun, napofe and zuzalan is still possible (12 possibilities). That leaves 15 in total.

Testing fusinun, napofe, pukenon and somonil splits these about evenly:
- **Lights up (8 left):** needs one with pukenon–somonil, pukenon–mesuvir or somonil–mesuvir; or needs two with fusinun–pukenon, fusinun–somonil, napofe–pukenon, napofe–somonil or pukenon–somonil.
- **Stays off (7 left):** needs two with fusinun–mesuvir, napofe–mesuvir, zuzalan–pukenon, zuzalan–somonil, zuzalan–mesuvir, pukenon–mesuvir or somonil–mesuvir.

TEST: fusinun, napofe, pukenon, somonil
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Eight possibilities remain:
- **Needs one:** pukenon–somonil, pukenon–mesuvir or somonil–mesuvir.
- **Needs two:** fusinun–pukenon, fusinun–somonil, napofe–pukenon, napofe–somonil or pukenon–somonil.

Testing fusinun, pukenon and mesuvir splits these 4 and 4:
- **Lights up:** all three "needs one" options, plus "needs two" with fusinun–pukenon.
- **Stays off:** "needs two" with fusinun–somonil, napofe–pukenon, napofe–somonil or pukenon–somonil.

TEST: fusinun, pukenon, mesuvir
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Four possibilities remain:
- **Needs one:** pukenon–somonil, pukenon–mesuvir or somonil–mesuvir.
- **Needs two:** fusinun–pukenon.

Testing pukenon alone splits these 2 and 2:
- **Lights up:** "needs one" with pukenon–somonil or pukenon–mesuvir.
- **Stays off:** "needs one" with somonil–mesuvir, or "needs two" with fusinun–pukenon.

Either way, one more test will be enough to settle it.

TEST: pukenon
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Pukenon lighting up alone means the machine needs only one nexiom and pukenon is one of the two. Two options remain: pukenon–somonil or pukenon–mesuvir.

Testing somonil alone will decide it. If it lights up, the pair is pukenon–somonil; if it stays off, the pair is pukenon–mesuvir.

TEST: somonil
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Somonil on its own stayed off, so it is not a nexiom. That leaves pukenon and mesuvir, and the machine needs only one nexiom to light up.

This matches every result:
- **Test 1:** fusinun, napofe and zuzalan stayed off because no nexiom was on the machine.
- **Tests 2, 3 and 4:** the machine lit up each time because pukenon was on it.
- **Test 5:** somonil alone stayed off.

ANSWER: nexioms = pukenon, mesuvir; needs = one
